restoration_note: The kephalaion narrates the First Man's molding into the garment of nature, the Living Spirit's capture of darkness's elements as cosmic storehouses, and the extraction of captive light leaving Hyle a corpse-body. The arc tracks one analogy: as the soul's departure leaves the body inert, so the drawing-out of the Living Soul reduces Hyle to the Death of the Midst. Most editor fills are tightly constrained by recurring formulas — ⲧⲁⲙⲓⲟⲛ (storehouses), ⲁⲛⲝⲱⲭ (wellsprings), ⲧⲱⲕ ⲁⲣⲉⲧϩ (standing-fast), ⲉⲛⲉⲣⲅⲓⲁ (operation) — and accepted with confidence. Gap 16 was corrected: the editor proposed ⲟⲛ ('again'), but ⲛⲛⲧⲁⲙ{16} clearly demands ⲓⲟⲛ to complete ⲧⲁⲙⲓⲟⲛ. The dense damage in lines 31–46 (the body-likeness application) and the entire closing section (lines 61–71) preserves too few traces to constrain fills; these are marked unrestorable rather than smoothly invented. The body-storehouse/soul-light correspondence governs every fill, with the controlled vocabulary set by the lexicon's entries for storehouse, body, soul, Hyle, and operation.
